.. _vs-concurrent-query:

===========================================
Parallelize Query Execution Across Segments
===========================================

.. default-domain:: mongodb

.. meta::
   :keywords: concurrent option, intra-query parallelism, concurrent segment search, single-threaded query, tail latency, query throughput, vector search, code example
   :description: Learn how the concurrent option in MongoDB Vector Search parallelizes each query across segments, and when to disable intra-query parallelism to reduce tail latency.

.. facet::
   :name: genre
   :values: reference

.. facet::
   :name: target_product
   :values: atlas

   .. facet::
      :name: sub_product
      :values: atlas-vector-search

.. contents:: On this page
   :local:
   :backlinks: none
   :depth: 2
   :class: singlecol

The ``concurrent`` option controls intra-query parallelism, which
{+avs+} enables by default. In this mode, {+avs+} utilizes more
resources, but improves each individual query latency. You can set
``concurrent`` to ``false`` to run a query single-threaded.

.. _vs-concurrent-limitations:

``concurrent`` Option Limitations
---------------------------------

When you run queries with the ``concurrent`` option, {+avs+} doesn't
guarantee that each query will be executed concurrently. For example,
when too many concurrent queries are queued, {+avs+} might fallback to
single-threaded execution. 

.. _vs-concurrent-syntax:

Syntax 
------

``concurrent`` has the following syntax:

.. code-block:: json
   :emphasize-lines: 8

   {
     "$vectorSearch": {  
       "index": "<index name>", 
       "path": "<field-to-search>",
       "queryVector": [<array-of-numbers>],
       "numCandidates": <number-of-candidates>,
       "limit": <number-of-results>,
       "concurrent": true | false,
       ...
     }
   }

.. _vs-concurrent-behavior:

Behavior 
--------

The ``concurrent`` boolean option controls whether {+avs+} parallelizes
query execution across segments, which, in many cases, improves the
response time. You can set one of the following values for the
``concurrent`` option:

- ``true`` - to request {+avs+} to run the query multi-threaded
  (default)
- ``false`` - to run the query single-threaded

If you omit the ``concurrent`` option, {+avs+} runs the query
multi-threaded.

{+avs+} provides you control over this behavior on a per-query basis so
that you can disable concurrent execution for light queries, which
minimizes contention and improves overall query throughput.
Concurrent execution is especially efficient on large datasets with many segments, and for heavy queries that use
large ``numCandidates`` values.

Consider setting ``concurrent`` to ``false`` if your workload has a
high query rate that saturates CPU. For these workloads, disabling
intra-query parallelism can increase peak throughput and reduce tail
latency.

.. _vs-concurrent-example:

Example 
-------

Consider the following query against the
:ref:`sample_mflix.embedded_movies <sample-mflix>` collection in the
sample data. The query disables concurrent search for movies with plots
similar to ``a fun and adventurous road trip``.
